page.title: StreamYard vs LiveKit for Virtual Events
page.description: Compare StreamYard's browser-based studio and LiveKit's realtime infrastructure for webinars, summits and hybrid productions with a practical buyer's checklist.
page.h1: StreamYard or LiveKit: which fits your virtual event?
page.definition: StreamYard is a browser-based streaming studio that handles switching, overlays and multi-platform distribution without code. LiveKit is an open-source realtime infrastructure platform that developers use to build custom video, audio and data applications with WebRTC.
page.quick_answer: Choose StreamYard when you need a ready-to-use broadcast studio for webinars and social streams. Choose LiveKit when you need programmable realtime infrastructure for custom virtual venues, spatial audio or embedded video in your own product.

sections.h2: What is the core difference between StreamYard and LiveKit?

blocks.p: StreamYard is a managed broadcast studio; LiveKit is a programmable realtime infrastructure. StreamYard runs in the browser, handles RTMP ingest, multi-stream to YouTube, LinkedIn, Facebook, and provides overlays, lower thirds, and guest links without installation. LiveKit provides SDKs and a self-hosted or cloud SFU for WebRTC, letting developers build custom rooms, spatial audio, data channels, and recording pipelines inside their own application.

sections.h2: Which platform fits a marketing webinar versus a custom virtual venue?

blocks.p: StreamYard fits marketing webinars and social broadcasts; LiveKit fits custom virtual venues and embedded video products.

sections.h2: How do setup time and technical requirements compare?

blocks.p: StreamYard launches in minutes with no code; LiveKit requires development effort and infrastructure decisions.

sections.h2: What are the pricing models and hidden costs?

blocks.p: StreamYard uses monthly seat licences; LiveKit charges for cloud minutes or self-hosted infrastructure.

sections.h2: Can you use StreamYard and LiveKit together in one production?

blocks.p: Yes, StreamYard can ingest a LiveKit room via RTMP or WHIP for broadcast while LiveKit powers the custom venue. A common pattern runs the interactive venue on LiveKit — spatial networking, breakout rooms, custom UI — then pushes a composed RTMP stream from a LiveKit Egress worker into StreamYard for multi-platform distribution, overlays, and cloud recording. This splits interactive logic from broadcast polish.

sections.h2: Who owns the production workload on each platform?

blocks.p: StreamYard shifts production to the host; LiveKit shifts it to the engineering team.

faq.q: Does StreamYard support custom RTMP destinations beyond the major platforms?
faq.a: StreamYard supports custom RTMP outputs on paid plans, letting you send to any ingest endpoint including a LiveKit Egress worker, a private CDN, or a hybrid encoder. You configure the server URL and stream key in the destination settings before going live.

faq.q: Can LiveKit replace StreamYard for a simple weekly webinar?
faq.a: LiveKit can power a simple webinar but you must build the host interface, guest lobby, recording, and multi-platform streaming yourself or adopt a prebuilt sample. For a recurring marketing webinar with no engineering bandwidth, StreamYard is faster to operate.

faq.q: What happens if the internet drops during a StreamYard broadcast?
faq.a: StreamYard records locally in each guest's browser and uploads when connectivity returns. The host sees a reconnecting indicator. For mission-critical events, run a parallel backup stream from a hardware encoder or a second StreamYard instance on a separate connection.

faq.q: Is LiveKit Cloud HIPAA or SOC two compliant for regulated events?
faq.a: LiveKit Cloud offers SOC two Type two and HIPAA-eligible configurations on dedicated clusters with a business associate agreement. Self-hosted deployments inherit your own infrastructure compliance. Verify the current attestation scope before committing regulated workloads.

faq.q: How do you rehearse speakers on each platform?
faq.a: StreamYard provides a private rehearsal mode with the same studio controls; guests join via link without going live. LiveKit rehearsal requires a staging environment or a separate room name in your application. Schedule one full rehearsal on the real platform two to five days before the event.
